metric.why: Idle servers burn power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing. Fleet utilization is where the money hides in most enterprise estates, and it is the denominator that makes every efficiency metric honest.
metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate is the share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak. It is the denominator that makes every efficiency metric honest.

The distinction between time-averaged and peak measurement is the whole point. A fleet sized for its busiest hour and idle the rest of the day carries power, licenses, and depreciation that produce nothing. Utilization measured over time exposes that gap. Utilization measured at peak hides it, because peak is the one moment the estate was built to satisfy.

For AI specifically, this sits alongside stranded power and space per cabinet and floor loading limits as a capacity question. The data does not say how utilization is measured, what counts as real work, or what rate is good. It defines the metric and its rationale, and stops there.
